# Sammādiṭṭhi Sutta (MN 9 (PTS MN i 46))

**ID:** MN 9 (PTS MN i 46)  
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Sammādiṭṭhi Sutta  
**PTS:** MN i 46  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0201m.mul0.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0201m.mul0.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sammādiṭṭhi Sutta* (MN 9) is delivered by the Venerable Sāriputta to his fellow mendicants, providing a comprehensive, systematic exposition of right view (*sammādiṭṭhi*), the initial factor of the noble eightfold path [Bodhi 2005]. Typical of Sāriputta's analytical teaching method, the discourse proceeds by dissecting the topic into fine components rather than employing literary embellishment [Nyanaponika, Hecker, and Bodhi 2003]. He elaborates sixteen distinct aspects of right view, treating unwholesome and wholesome action along with their respective roots, the four nutriments (*āhāra*), the four noble truths, the twelve factors of dependent origination (*paṭiccasamuppāda*) with analytical definitions (such as defining mentality, *nāma*, at MN 9.54), and the taints (*āsava*) as conditions for ignorance [Ñāṇamoli and Bodhi 1995; Thakchoe and Garfield 2007]. Its commentary differentiates right view into conceptual understanding conforming to the truths (*saccānulomika-sammādiṭṭhi*) and experiential wisdom directly penetrating them (*saccapaṭivedha-sammādiṭṭhi*) [Bodhi 2005; Thakchoe and Garfield 2007].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Full parallels: SA 344 拘絺羅
- Passage-level parallels: DN 22 (PTS DN ii 290) Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna Sutta; MN 10 (PTS MN i 55) Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna Sutta
- Resembling parallels: AN 9.13 Koṭṭhikasutta; MA 29 大拘絺羅; SF 172 Dṛṣṭisampanna

**Sources**

- [Bodhi 2005] Bhikkhu Bodhi, In the Buddha's Words: An Anthology of Discourses from the Pali Canon (2005) — Role as a monastic primer and commentarial division of right view.
- [Nyanaponika, Hecker, and Bodhi 2003] Nyanaponika Thera, Hellmuth Hecker, and Bhikkhu Bodhi, Great Disciples of the Buddha (2003) — Analysis of Sāriputta's expository and dissective teaching style in MN 9.
- [Thakchoe and Garfield 2007] Sonam Thakchoe and Jay L. Garfield, Two Truths Debate: Tsongkhapa and Gorampa on the Middle Way (2007) — Sixteen aspects of right view and nutriments listed in the sutta.
- [Ñāṇamoli and Bodhi 1995] Bhikkhu Ñāṇamoli and Bhikkhu Bodhi, The Middle Length Discourses of the Buddha (1995) — Factorial analysis of dependent origination and definition of mentality (nāma).
- [Nyanaponika Thera 1976] Nyanaponika Thera, Abhidhamma Studies: Researches in Buddhist Psychology (3rd ed., 1976) — Mentions Bhikkhu Soma's translation and commentary title.
- [Heim 2014] Maria Heim, Forerunner of All Things: Buddhaghosa on Mind, Intention, and Agency (2014) — Cites Ñāṇamoli's translation of the sutta and its commentary.
- [Anālayo 2016] Bhikkhu Anālayo, Mindfully Facing Disease and Death (2016) — Notes comparative studies on the Samyukta-āgama parallel to MN 9.
